rationale: Both are project/work-management platforms used to plan work, assign tasks, track progress, and coordinate teams. They are plausible alternatives for a team selecting a central project-management tool.

Salesforce is centered on CRM and a broad customer platform, while Intercom's primary positioning centers on customer messaging and support automation. Some customer-workflow overlap exists, but they are not direct substitutes across their primary jobs.

HubSpot's core suite covers CRM, marketing, sales, and service workflows; Intercom focuses on customer messaging and support automation. They can overlap in customer engagement, but a full-suite CRM and a messaging/support platform are not direct replacements by default.

Miro is primarily a visual collaboration canvas for workshops, brainstorming, and diagrams; Basecamp is a project-management and team communication workspace. Teams may use both together rather than choose one as a substitute for the other.

Figma centers on collaborative interface/product design and prototyping, while Vercel provides web application deployment and frontend cloud infrastructure. Their roles in a product-development workflow are complementary.

Airtable centers on structured data, configurable apps, and workflow building; Basecamp centers on project coordination and team communication. Some teams could use either for lightweight tracking, but their primary jobs differ.
